builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI
summary: SimXAI replaces the GUS-style pipeline (intent recognition, dialogue management, template-based generation) of conversational XAI agents with a single tool-calling LLM that routes to existing XAI resources. It costs LLM inference (API or a small local model on the 24 GB GPU) plus implementation of tool schemas for the underlying XAI methods, and removes the modular GUS components. It can fail through incorrect tool selection on ambiguous or context-dependent queries, unfaithful responses if the LLM deviates from tool outputs, and dependence on the availability and correctness of the external XAI resources it calls.
rationale: The approach matches constrained infrastructure since it needs only an API or small LLM plus tool glue code, but its function-selection accuracy and faithfulness must be validated on the reader's specific XAI workload and user queries before production adoption.
technique: LLM tool-calling layer for conversational XAI

It costs LLM inference (API or a small local model on the 24 GB GPU) plus implementation of tool schemas for the underlying XAI methods, and removes the modular GUS components.
